Therefore, the gods are the principles of all species; these are followed by the gods whose prince is <term>ousia</term> <gloss>essence</gloss>. These sensible ones are of both origins and are alike, and through sensible nature, they finish all things. One illuminates its work through the other. The heaven, or whatever is comprehended by that name, is the <term>ousiarches</term> <gloss>ruler of essence</gloss>, Jupiter. For through heaven, Jupiter offers life to all. The <term>ousiarches</term> of the sun is light. For the good of light is infused into us through the orb of the sun. Of the thirty-six stars (whose name is Horoscopes) fixed always in the same place, their <term>ousiarches</term> or prince is he whom they call <term>Pantomorph</term> <gloss>all-formed</gloss> or Omniform. He creates diverse forms for diverse species. The seven spheres which are called erratic have their <term>ousiarchas</term> <gloss>rulers of essence</gloss>, that is, their princes, whom they call Fortune, <term>eimarmenē</term> <gloss>fate/destiny</gloss>, by which all things are changed, by the most firm law of the stability of nature, and varied by eternal agitation. Truly, the air is the organ, or machine of all things, through which all things are made. Moreover, the second <term>ousiarches</term> of this is for mortals, mortal things, and things similar to these. Therefore, with things being thus, moving from the lowest to the highest, all things pertaining to themselves are naturally connected to one another, so that mortal things are annexed to mortal things, and sensible things to sensible things. Truly, the highest of the governance obeys that highest Lord, so that it is not many, or rather it is one. For all things depend from the one, flowing down from it: when they are distant, they are believed to be many, separated. But when united, they are one, or rather two: whence all things are made, and by whom they are made. That is, from the matter of which they are made, and from His will, by whose nod other things are effected. ASCLEPIUS: Is this again the reason, O Trismegistus? TRISMEGISTUS: Such it is, O Asclepius.
